hypothesis: Cooperatively stage each 256-source tile's x, y, z, and mass values in 4 KiB of static shared memory so the block's output threads reuse them instead of repeatedly fetching those source fields from global memory. The sequential pairwise arithmetic and one-output-per-active-thread strategy remain close to baseline; barriers and shared-memory occupancy costs may offset the reduced global loads, so this is a performance hypothesis for measurement.
notes: The default launch geometry is unchanged. Tile loading covers full and tail tiles; both barriers are reached by every thread, including inactive output lanes, and only active lanes write outputs. Static shared storage is 4,096 bytes, below the supplied 49,152-byte limit; launch.json's dynamic shared-memory setting remains unchanged. The supplied baseline is correct with mean_seconds 0.0018503532502855123, but this candidate has not been measured; controller correctness and timing results are required before drawing a performance conclusion.
transformations: Stage source x, y, z, and mass in four 256-element shared-memory arrays, loading each tile cooperatively.
Synchronize after tile loads and after tile consumption so all output lanes, including tail-block lanes, safely participate before shared storage is reused.
Keep the source-particle accumulation in ascending tile/source order and guard output work and writes with i < n.
